inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Child/Caregiver Ratio - 18 Months Difference in Age: I observed four children in the toddler classroom. The youngest child was 9 months and the oldest child in the room was 2 years and 4 months old.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/Caregiver Ratio - 18 Months Difference in Age (26 TAC §746.1605(1))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: During today's inspection a four year old child left the classroom unsupervised.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Medication No Longer Used: Expired medication was stored at the operation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Medication No Longer Used (26 TAC §746.3809)

occurrences.finding: Children's Records Maintained: Children's records were evaluated for six children enrolled and the following was determined:    Current immunization records are needed for three children enrolled. The admission date is needed for one child enrolled. School information such as name and phone number is needed for two children enrolled.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records Maintained (26 TAC §746.603(a))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: Based on the information obtained during the course of this investigation it was determined a caregiver used prohibited punishment when grabbing and pulling a child in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: Based on the information obtained during the course of this investigation, it was determined a caregiver did not demonstrate good judgment when using their foot to move a child across the floor.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Documentation of Training Requirements - Trainer's Name: Training certificates reviewed during today's inspection did not show the participants name and date of training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documentation of Training Requirements - Trainer's Name (26 TAC §746.1329(b)(4))

occurrences.finding: Immunization Records, Exceptions, and Exemptions Current: An updated immunization record is needed for one child in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Immunization Records, Exceptions, and Exemptions Current (26 TAC §746.613(b))

occurrences.finding: Children Handwashing Before Eating: Children did not wash their hands before eating.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Handwashing Before Eating (26 TAC §746.3417(1))

occurrences.finding: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering: During today's inspection a caregiver did not wash a child's hands after diapering.     Note: This was corrected during inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering (26 TAC §746.3417(3))

occurrences.finding: Diapering Procedures - Sanitizing Diaper Changing Area: A caregiver did not sanitize the diaper-changing surface after diapering children in care. Note: This was corrected during inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Diapering Procedures - Sanitizing Diaper Changing Area (26 TAC §746.3505(e))

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Orientation: A caregiver was observed caring for a group of three children ages 18 months-2 years old. The caregiver had not completed orientation training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Orientation (26 TAC §746.1301(a)(1)(A))

occurrences.finding: Basic Requirements for Infants - Free from Choking Objects That May Cause Choking in Infants or Toddlers: An infant was observed with a pacifier attatched to her clothing by a cloth like string while asleep in the crib.     Note: The pacifier was removed during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Basic Requirements for Infants - Free from Choking Objects That May Cause Choking in Infants or Toddlers (26 TAC §746.2401(6))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A child was observed wandering the hallway without a caregiver present.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for: A Caregiver did not know the number of children in the school age classroom during the inspection. The caregiver stated there were 12 children and there was only 10 children in the classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Discipline - Teaches Acceptable Behavior and Self-control: Based on the information obtained, it was determined the operations discipline methods does not teach acceptable behavior and self-control.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Discipline - Teaches Acceptable Behavior and Self-control (26 TAC §746.2803(3))

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric CPR: Three caregivers are in need of Pediatric CPR training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric CPR (26 TAC §746.1315(b))

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking.: Three caregivers are in need of Pediatric First Aid training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking. (26 TAC §746.1315(a))

occurrences.finding: Sign-in and Sign-out Tracking System: The sign in and out log was reviewed and showed eight of nine children signed in.     Note: This was corrected during inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Sign-in and Sign-out Tracking System (26 TAC §746.631(a))

occurrences.finding: Documentation of Drills: There was no documentation showing the fire extinguishers and carbon detectors were inspected monthly.    Note: This was corrected at inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documentation of Drills (26 TAC §746.5205(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Group Responsible For: The caregiver in the toddler classroom was unaware of the number of children present in the room. The caregiver stated 11 children were present, however 10 were present in the room.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Group Responsible For (26 TAC §746.1203(2))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Admission Information: Records were evaluated for six   children enrolled and the following   was determined:  5 of 6 needed a special needs statement.  5 of 6 needed immunization records.  3 of 6 needed a health statement.  3 of 6 needed emergency contact information.  1 of 6 needed emergency care info.  1 of 6 needed food allergy information.  1 of 6 needed the admission date.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Admission Information (26 TAC §746.603(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: The infant caregiver was observed caring for five infants age 6 months, 7 months, 11 months, 11 months, and 17 months. The specified age group was 0-11 months. The caregiver was out of ratio by one child.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: Policies Comply with Rules: The operational policies were reviewed and the following policies were not included:        -Parent approval not needed for visitation.   -Promotion of indoor and outdoor physical activity:  	-The benefits of physical activity and outdoor play.  	- The duration of indoor and outdoor physical activity at your operation.  	-The type of physical activity (structured and unstructured) that children may engage in at your operation.  	-Each setting in which your physical activity program will take place.  	-A plan to ensure physical activity occurs on days when extreme weather conditions prohibit or limit outdoor play.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Policies Comply with Rules (26 TAC §746.201(1))

occurrences.finding: Infant Daily Report - Times and Amount of Food: During the inspection the infant daily reports were observed for five infants. No information as documented although infants were observed sleeping and during feedings.    Note: The permit holder updated the reports during inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Infant Daily Report - Times and Amount of Food (26 TAC §746.2431(2))

occurrences.finding: Crib Mattress Cover - Snug-Fitting and Thin: Four cribs in the infant classroom needed snug-fitting sheets.     Note: The permit holder taped the bottom of the sheets to the mattress.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Crib Mattress Cover - Snug-Fitting and Thin (26 TAC §746.2415(c)(2))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Children's Names and Ages: The volunteer in the infant classroom was unaware of the children's ages in the classroom. The volunteer was asked to provide documentation showing the ages but could not.     Note: The permit holder provided information showing the ages of the children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Children's Names and Ages (26 TAC §746.1203(3))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Admission Information: Records were evaluated for six children enrolled and the following was determined:    5 of 6 needed a special needs statement.  5 of 6 needed immunization records.   3 of 6 needed a health statement.  3 of 6 needed emergency contact information.  1 of 6 needed emergency care info.  1 of 6 needed food allergy information.  1 of 6 needed the admission date.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Admission Information (26 TAC §746.603(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Using Inappropriate Long Period of Silence or Inactivity Including Requiring Child to Remain in a Restrictive Device: A child in the 2-5 year old classroom was placed in a high chair as a form of discipline and guidance. The child was placed in the high chair due to throwing crayons.     Note: The child was removed from the high chair during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Using Inappropriate Long Period of Silence or Inactivity Including Requiring Child to Remain in a Restrictive Device (26 TAC §746.2805(10))

occurrences.finding: Minimum Qualifications Child Care Center Employees and Caregivers - Affidavit: A notarized affidavit was needed for one volunteer.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Minimum Qualifications Employees and Caregivers - Affidavit (Form 2985) (26 TAC §746.1105(3))

occurrences.finding: Infant May Not Sleep in a Restrictive Device: A three month old was observed sleeping in a bouncer during this inspection.     I observed an eleven month old sleeping in a bouncer during this inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Infant May Not Sleep in a Restrictive Device (26 TAC §746.2426)

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Free of other activities: When entering the infant classroom I observed the infant volunteer on her cell phone.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Free of other activities (26 TAC §746.1203(6))

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days: Updated feeding instructions are needed for one infant in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days (26 TAC §746.2421(b))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: A group of 8 children age 2-5 years old was left unsupervised upon my arrival.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children (26 TAC §746.1203(4))

occurrences.finding: Substitutes, Volunteers and Contractors - Unqualified Not Left Alone with Children: I observed a volunteer who does not meet caregiver qualifications alone in the infant classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Substitutes, Volunteers and Contractors - Unqualified Not Left Alone with Children (26 TAC §746.1401(f))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: I observed a volunteer pick up an 11 month old by one arm.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: A volunteer was observed caring for five infants age 3 months, 6 months, 7 months, 11 months, and 17 months. The specified age group was 0-11 months. The volunteer was out of ratio by one child.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: Policies Comply with Rules: The operational policies were reviewed and the following policies were not included:      -Suspension and expulsion policy  -Enrollment procedures, including how and when parents will be notified of policy changes.  -Transportation procedures.   -Parent approval not needed for visitation.   -Promotion of indoor and outdoor physical activity:  	-The benefits of physical activity and outdoor play.  	- The duration of indoor and outdoor physical activity at your operation.  	-The type of physical activity (structured and unstructured) that children may engage in at your operation.  	-Each setting in which your physical activity program will take place.  	-A plan to ensure physical activity occurs on days when extreme weather conditions prohibit or limit outdoor play.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Policies Comply with Rules (26 TAC §746.201(1))

occurrences.finding: Emergency Preparedness Plan - Communication Procedures: The Emergency Preparedness Plan was reviewed and did not include the following:    -Evacuation diagram  -Procedures for evacuating and relocating children who are under 24 months of age, who have limited mobility, or who otherwise may need assistance.  -The emergency telephone number that is on file with us.  - How you will communicate with local authorities (such as fire, law enforcement, emergency medical services, health department), parents and Child Care Regulation.   -How your staff will continue to care for the children until each child has been released.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Emergency Preparedness Plan - Communication Procedures (26 TAC §746.5202(2))

occurrences.finding: Emergency Evacuation and Relocation Diagram - Designated Location: The evacuation and relocation diagram posted did not indicate the relocation address.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Emergency Evacuation and Relocation Diagram - Designated Location (26 TAC §746.5207(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Policies Comply with Rules: The operational policies were reviewed and the following policies were not included:      -Suspension and expulsion policy  -Enrollment procedures, including how and when parents will be notified of policy changes.  -Transportation procedures.   -Parent approval not needed for visitation.   -Promotion of indoor and outdoor physical activity:  	-The benefits of physical activity and outdoor play.  	- The duration of indoor and outdoor physical activity at your operation.  	-The type of physical activity (structured and unstructured) that children may engage in at your operation.  	-Each setting in which your physical activity program will take place.  	-A plan to ensure physical activity occurs on days when extreme weather conditions prohibit or limit outdoor play.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Policies Comply with Rules (26 TAC §746.201(1))

occurrences.finding: Emergency Preparedness Plan - Communication Procedures: The Emergency Preparedness Plan was reviewed and did not include the following:    -Evacuation diagram  -Procedures for evacuating and relocating children who are under 24 months of age, who have limited mobility, or who otherwise may need assistance.  -The emergency telephone number that is on file with us.  - How you will communicate with local authorities (such as fire, law enforcement, emergency medical services, health department), parents and Child Care Regulation.   -How your staff will continue to care for the children until each child has been released.      -The operation has two relocation sites listed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Emergency Preparedness Plan - Communication Procedures (26 TAC §746.5202(2))
